source.note: No comparable figure is recorded. The record carried 76.5 mW/cm2, relayed from a search summary as an average across the panel face with no distance at all, and the page does not show that number. What the page shows is an irradiance table giving more than 170 and more than 68 at six inches, marked ** and * respectively, with footnotes labelling * as consumer-grade and ** as laboratory. Its own prose says the consumer readings are the higher ones, which contradicts the footnotes, so the page does not settle which method produced which number. Nothing here read a report behind either. This catalogue's irradiance field carries one unqualified figure and compares it against other products' unqualified figures, so importing either number would assert both a method and a comparability the source does not support. Read from the 1500+ column of the series comparison table. The series page also sells the 300+, the 1500X and array bundles, and none of their figures belong on this record.
